question: Is it worth paying for a dedicated memory product for my agent, or should it just search the raw transcript?

sentences.text: The most direct item compares dedicated memory products (Mem0, Zep) and BM25 against keeping raw history that the agent searches itself, run across three coding agents and three models while recording what every rollout costs.
That excerpt poses whether designed memory still helps once the model can search for itself, but it reports no result, so it supports no buy-or-not verdict on its own.

Complementary work argues a memory's value is task-conditioned, helping more when it actually contains the information the later question needs, and that this utility should be read next to a cost ledger covering formation, storage and exposure.
So the evidence supports treating the choice as a per-task measurement of utility against cost rather than a blanket case for paying for a memory product.

question: Could a made-up news story make AI traders all sell at the same time?

sentences.text: Yes: because LLM trading agents read the same news feeds under near-identical policies, a single fabricated post can push them into the same trade at the same moment.
This is framed as information injection, which targets the evidence an agent trusts rather than its instructions, and it is studied across five injection vectors and seven event categories.
The risk is consequential because AI trading agents operate in continuously changing markets where news is used as evidence for real capital decisions.

question: When should a live assistant stay quiet while walking someone through a job?

sentences.text: A live assistant should stay quiet until it has evidence that a step is complete or a mistake has occurred, rather than speaking on a timer.
It should not rely on a fixed silence before speaking, because that can interrupt users who pause mid-utterance or respond late to those who have finished.
It may also stay quiet about details the user already knows, saving time and attention for what happens next.
